identification.summary: North Korean state-sponsored actor focused on stealing cryptocurrency, usually by socially engineering developers and staff at blockchain firms and their vendors [S1][S3]. US government advisories track the same activity as TraderTraitor [S1][S3][S5]. In July 2023 GitHub, which Microsoft owns, named Jade Sleet as the actor behind a social-engineering campaign that used repository invitations and malicious npm dependencies [S1][S2]. The FBI has tied TraderTraitor to the theft of about $308 million from DMM Bitcoin in 2024 and about $1.5 billion from Bybit in February 2025 [S5][S6]. Reporting in 2026 links the actor to the KelpDAO/LayerZero bridge exploit and to an intrusion at an India-based IT services firm that used macOS backdoors [S9][S10][S12].
identification.firstObserved: US advisory AA22-108A (April 2022) describes TraderTraitor activity since at least 2020 [S3]. The Microsoft/GitHub public naming of Jade Sleet dates to July 2023 [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Jade Sleet (in-development name Storm-0954). Microsoft's naming map lists LABYRINTH CHOLLIMA (CrowdStrike) as an alias [S13]. GitHub equated Jade Sleet with CISA's TraderTraitor [S1]. FBI statements on the DMM Bitcoin and Bybit thefts list Jade Sleet, UNC4899 and Slow Pisces as other names for TraderTraitor [S5][S6]. Mandiant says UNC4899 likely corresponds to TraderTraitor [S4]. Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 tracks the activity as Slow Pisces [S8]. AA22-108A groups TraderTraitor under the broader Lazarus Group / APT38 / BlueNoroff umbrella [S3]. Keep that umbrella separate from this specific cluster. MITRE ATT&CK has no Group ID assigned in this record.

attribution.sponsor: Democratic People's Republic of Korea. Mandiant assesses UNC4899 as a cryptocurrency-focused element within the DPRK Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB) [S4].
attribution.confidence: The FBI publicly attributed the Bybit theft (2025-02-26 PSA) and the DMM Bitcoin theft (December 2024, with DC3 and Japan's National Police Agency) to TraderTraitor, i.e. to North Korea [S5][S6]. Mandiant assesses with high confidence that UNC4899 is an RGB element, and assesses that UNC4899 'likely' corresponds to TraderTraitor [S4]. In coverage of the LayerZero incident report, Mandiant and CrowdStrike attribute the KelpDAO operation to TraderTraitor/UNC4899 [S10]. GitHub attributed the July 2023 campaign to Jade Sleet [S1].
attribution.basis: Joint FBI/CISA/Treasury advisory AA22-108A [S3]. FBI attributions of specific thefts [S5][S6]. Mandiant incident response, including an OPSEC slip in which UNC4899 connected directly from a Pyongyang netblock during the JumpCloud intrusion [S4]. GitHub/Microsoft telemetry [S1]. Vendor reporting from Unit 42, Safe{Wallet}/Mandiant and LayerZero [S7][S8][S10].

objectives: Revenue generation for the DPRK state through theft of cryptocurrency from exchanges, DeFi protocols, wallet and custody providers, and individuals [S3][S5][S6]. The actor also gains access to software and service providers so it can compromise their downstream cryptocurrency customers [S4][S7].

sectors: Cryptocurrency wallet and custody software providers [S5][S7]
Play-to-earn gaming and crypto-focused venture capital [S3]
Identity/SaaS service providers used as supply-chain pivots [S4]
IT services, DevOps and fintech personnel [S12]
targeting.notes: The actor targets people more than perimeter devices. Developers, DevOps engineers and executives at crypto firms or their suppliers are approached through fake recruiter or developer personas on LinkedIn, GitHub, Slack and Telegram [S1][S2][S5][S8][S12]. GitHub said most targets were connected to blockchain, cryptocurrency or online gambling, with a few in cybersecurity [S1].

capabilities.summary: Social engineering through fake recruiters and developers, using job-interview 'coding challenges' and repository invitations. These lead victims to clone and run trojanized projects or malicious npm dependencies [S1][S2][S5][S8]. AA22-108A describes trojanized cryptocurrency applications for Windows and macOS [S3]. The actor runs supply-chain operations: it compromised JumpCloud's commands framework to reach downstream customers [S4], and it compromised a Safe{Wallet} developer laptop, hijacking AWS session tokens to bypass MFA and tamper with front-end JavaScript that Bybit signers used [S7]. Unit 42 documents gated, in-memory payload delivery (RN Loader, RN Stealer) that steals SSH keys and AWS, Kubernetes and Google Cloud configuration files from macOS hosts [S8]. Mandiant observed macOS keychain theft and persistence through backdoors and plist files within 24 hours of access [S4]. In 2026 the actor used a booby-trapped Terraform project with typosquatted provider registries, plus Rust macOS backdoors: FLATROOF (Telegram exfiltration) and ROOFDECK (Nostr-relay C2) [S12]. It also manipulated RPC responses and ran DDoS against healthy nodes to defeat a bridge verifier [S10]. After thefts, the actor quickly launders funds across thousands of addresses and multiple blockchains [S6].

campaigns.name: AA22-108A TraderTraitor advisory
campaigns.summary: The FBI, CISA and Treasury warn that a DPRK state-sponsored group, active since at least 2020, targets blockchain companies with trojanized crypto applications delivered through social engineering.

campaigns.name: JumpCloud supply-chain compromise
campaigns.summary: UNC4899 spear-phishes JumpCloud, abuses its commands framework to run a malicious Ruby script on a handful of crypto-sector customers (from 27 June 2023), and steals macOS keychain data.

campaigns.name: GitHub/npm social-engineering campaign
campaigns.summary: GitHub attributes a low-volume campaign to Jade Sleet. The actor used fake personas and repository invitations to get tech-industry employees to run malicious npm dependencies.

campaigns.name: DMM Bitcoin theft (~$308M)
campaigns.summary: A fake LinkedIn recruiter sends a Ginco employee a malicious Python 'pre-employment test', which leads to the theft of 4,502.9 BTC from DMM Bitcoin. The FBI attributed the theft in December 2024.

campaigns.name: Bybit theft (~$1.5B)
campaigns.summary: A compromised Safe{Wallet} developer machine and tampered front-end code let the actor alter a multisig transaction signed by Bybit. The FBI attributed the theft to TraderTraitor on 2025-02-26.

campaigns.name: Slow Pisces coding-challenge campaign
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 reports LinkedIn recruiter lures that lead to GitHub 'coding challenges' delivering RN Loader and RN Stealer to crypto developers.

campaigns.name: KelpDAO rsETH / LayerZero exploit (~$292M)
campaigns.summary: A LayerZero Labs developer is socially engineered from 6 March 2026. RPC responses are later poisoned to drain about 116,500 rsETH. Mandiant and CrowdStrike attribute the operation to UNC4899.

campaigns.name: India IT services firm compromise (FLATROOF/ROOFDECK)
campaigns.summary: A fake job interview delivers a trojanized Terraform project to a DevOps engineer. Rust macOS backdoors trigger when the project is opened in the Cursor AI editor.

diamond.adversary: DPRK RGB-linked crypto-theft cluster (Jade Sleet / TraderTraitor / UNC4899 / Slow Pisces) [S1][S4][S5][S8].
diamond.capability: Recruiter and coding-challenge lures; trojanized repositories and npm packages; supply-chain compromise of SaaS and wallet providers; macOS stealers and backdoors (RN Loader, RN Stealer, FLATROOF, ROOFDECK); cloud session-token theft [S1][S4][S7][S8][S12].
diamond.infrastructure: Fake personas on LinkedIn, GitHub, Slack and Telegram; GitHub-hosted repositories; ORB proxy infrastructure (one direct connection from Pyongyang observed); typosquatted HashiCorp registries; Telegram and Nostr relays for C2 and exfiltration [S1][S4][S8][S12].
diamond.victim: Developers, DevOps staff and executives at crypto exchanges, DeFi/bridge protocols, wallet providers, and their IT and SaaS suppliers in the US, Japan, India and elsewhere [S1][S4][S5][S6][S12].
diamond.socioPolitical: Sanctions-evading revenue generation for the DPRK regime [S3][S6].
diamond.technology: Developer workstations (often macOS), package managers, CI/IaC tooling, cloud consoles and multisig signing front ends [S4][S7][S8][S12].

gaps: No Microsoft Threat Intelligence profile of Jade Sleet was found in the searches. The Microsoft-side description comes from GitHub's July 2023 post, and that post was not fetched directly (github.blog was unreachable); content comes from search summaries and SecurityWeek coverage [S1][S2].

Primary US government documents (AA22-108A, the FBI PSA on Bybit, the FBI/NPA statement on DMM Bitcoin) could not be opened. Their content here comes from search summaries and press coverage [S3][S5][S6].

The Microsoft naming map links LABYRINTH CHOLLIMA (CrowdStrike) to Jade Sleet [S13], but no CrowdStrike source was found confirming this mapping or naming the CrowdStrike designation used for Bybit or KelpDAO. Treat the CrowdStrike alias as unverified.

Mandiant hedges the UNC4899 = TraderTraitor equivalence as 'likely' [S4]. FBI statements treat Jade Sleet, UNC4899 and Slow Pisces as the same cluster [S5][S6]. Cluster boundaries may still differ between vendors.
Relationship to the broader Lazarus/APT38/BlueNoroff umbrella and to other Microsoft Sleet actors (e.g., Sapphire Sleet, Citrine Sleet, Moonstone Sleet) is not resolved in the sources gathered.

SentinelOne's original 2026 report on FLATROOF/ROOFDECK and LayerZero's primary incident report were not opened. Details come from the CSA research note and The Defiant [S10][S12]; the FLATROOF/ROOFDECK details were not corroborated in fact-check searches.
No MITRE ATT&CK Group ID is recorded for this cluster.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (operational environment): The relevant cyberspace terrain is the people layer (developers, DevOps engineers, executives) and the developer toolchain: GitHub, npm, Terraform/IaC registries, cloud session tokens and SaaS administration frameworks. Perimeter devices matter less [S1][S4][S7][S12]. STEP 2 (effects): Any DoD or DIB element with cryptocurrency, fintech, or third-party SaaS and identity dependencies inherits risk from supplier compromise. JumpCloud and Safe{Wallet} show one supplier compromise reaching many downstream victims [S4][S7]. STEP 3 (threat evaluation): The template is recruiter or developer persona, then trojanized repository or coding challenge, then macOS stealer or backdoor, then theft of cloud and SSH credentials, then supply-chain pivot or direct asset theft, then rapid multi-chain laundering [S4][S6][S8][S12]. STEP 4 (COAs): MLCOA is continued job-lure targeting of crypto, fintech and DevOps staff to fund the DPRK [S8]. MDCOA is applying the same developer-workstation and SaaS supply-chain tradecraft to an identity or IT provider serving defense customers; JumpCloud is the precedent [S4]. Candidate indicators: unsolicited 'coding test' repositories run on corporate hosts; unexpected npm or Terraform provider sources and typosquatted registries; Telegram or Nostr-relay traffic from developer Macs; anomalous use of cloud session tokens; SaaS command or agent frameworks executing unfamiliar scripts [S1][S4][S8][S12].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: Track supplier and SaaS compromise reporting, plus FBI attributions of crypto thefts, as early warning of the actor's current tradecraft. Its supply-chain intrusions reach downstream customers within days [S4][S6]. (2) Authorities: The activity sits largely in private-sector and FBI law-enforcement lanes [S5][S6]. DoD roles are mostly defending its own networks and supporting partners, so coordinate through the appropriate interagency channels. (3) Mission assurance: Developer and DevOps workstations, IaC pipelines and identity platforms should be treated as mission-relevant terrain. Brief cleared personnel on fake recruiter and coding-test lures [S8][S12]. (4) Coordination: Share indicators with DC3 and DIB partners; DC3 joined the DMM Bitcoin attribution [S5]. Expect vendor names (Jade Sleet, TraderTraitor, UNC4899, Slow Pisces) to differ across reports [S5][S6].
